name: Bilateral Symmetry Analysis
description: Detects and quantifies unnatural bilateral symmetry in images. AI generation models often exhibit an inductive bias toward perfect mirror symmetry, producing structural perfection that is statistically abnormal in authentic photographs of real-world scenes.
mechanism: Computes pixel-level and structural feature correlation between geometrically mirrored halves (left/right, top/bottom) of an image. The algorithm identifies symmetric constellations of features and calculates a global symmetry score using Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC). Unusually peak correlation scores indicate synthetic generation biases or cloning manipulations.
parameters: Comparison Metric: Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC), Feature Extraction: SIFT/SURF Keypoints, Transformation: Horizontal/Vertical Mirroring
accuracy: Moderate (65-75%) - Most effective when analyzing scenes that naturally lack perfect geometric symmetry (e.g., human faces, landscapes).
source: Loy & Eklundh (2006) / Mader et al. (2017) on synthetic symmetry biases
useCase: Identifying structural perfection artifacts commonly produced by generative models and evaluating the physical plausibility of the scene.

references.title: Loy, G. & Eklundh, J.O. (2006). Detecting Symmetry and Symmetric Constellations of Features. ECCV.

strengths:
• Computationally straightforward and fast.
• Captures a fundamental structural bias inherent to many generative networks.
• Functions without the need for large, dataset-specific training.
• Effective complementary metric to frequency and texture analysis.
limitations:
• Generates false positives in authentically symmetric scenes (e.g., architecture, reflections).
• Low standalone diagnostic confidence without contextual analysis.
• Easily circumvented by explicitly prompting the generative model for asymmetrical compositions.
• Highly sensitive to slight perspective distortions or subject rotation in authentic images.
